name: Jigarthanda
instructions: 1. Soak the badam pisin in water overnight until it expands into a jelly-like consistency.
2. Boil the milk in a heavy-bottomed pan, stirring constantly, and reduce it to half its volume until it thickens.
3. Add sugar and khoya (or condensed milk) to the boiling milk and stir until dissolved.
4. Allow the thickened milk to cool completely.
5. In a tall glass, add a generous spoonful of the prepared badam pisin jelly.
6. Pour the chilled thickened milk over the jelly and add a splash of nannari syrup.
7. Top the mixture with a large scoop of vanilla ice cream and serve immediately.
description: Originating from the city of Madurai, Jigarthanda translates to 'cool heart'. It is a traditional, refreshing summer drink prized for its natural cooling properties, attributed primarily to the use of almond gum (badam pisin).
